requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading immediately on node1.
requirements.summary: The module was initially absent, a persistent modprobe policy was installed, and an explicit load attempt was denied with return code 1 while the module remained absent.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage blocked after node1 reboots.
requirements.summary: Node1 was healthy before the restart, accepted the restart request, returned with a different boot identity, and recovered in a running state with no failed units and a writable root filesystem. After reboot, the policy remained present, usb_storage was absent, and an explicit load attempt was denied without loading it. The lifecycle boot observations independently confirm the boot-identity change.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. usb-storage was blocked immediately and remained blocked through an observed reboot. The mandatory node-restart protocol is coherent and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: No workload-specific data or multi-node cluster existed in the captured topology, so restart recovery evidence is limited to OS health, writable storage, retained configuration, and the required module behavior.

Testing used an explicit modprobe attempt rather than a physical USB-storage hot-plug event; the effective install-deny rule and post-reboot load failure nevertheless directly test kernel-module loading.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task roles: installing the modprobe policy, rebuilding the active initramfs, performing bounded load tests, and rebooting for persistence verification. Services, sockets, and package health remained healthy. The only unnecessary retained residue was two small diagnostic output files: /tmp/usb-storage-modprobe.out from cmd-467ce7f47a16451f and /tmp/usb-storage-postboot.out from cmd-5aaea1916d9241e5; neither was cleaned up.
